Rather, ﴿it was not for any messenger﴾, meaning any messenger whatsoever, ﴿to bring a sign﴾, whether a proposed sign, or a sign abrogating (naskh, abrogation) a ruling of his own law, or of a law before him, or otherwise, ﴿except by the permission of God﴾, meaning the One who encompasses everything in knowledge and power. For matters with Him are not without order, nor excessive in them, nor is anything of them lost. Rather, ﴿for every term﴾, meaning the limit of a matter that He alone decreed, so that there is a matter with Him, ﴿a Book﴾ in which He has recorded that such a matter will occur at such a time, of reward, punishment, rulings, and the bringing of signs and other things, by affirmation and abrogation according to what wisdom requires. Wisdom requires that for establishing prophethood a single miracle (mu'jizah) suffices, and whatever exceeds that is subject to His will.

Then He gave the reason for that by His saying: ﴿Allah effaces﴾, i.e., the Supreme King, ﴿whatever He wills﴾, i.e., of its effacement from the laws (sharai') and rulings (ahkam) and other things, through abrogation (naskh), so He lifts it; ﴿and establishes﴾ whatever He wills to establish of that, by letting it stand and its ruling remain in force, as He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Whatever verse We abrogate or cause to be forgotten [We bring a better or similar one]﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106], up to His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Do you not know that Allah is over all things competent?﴾ [al-Baqarah: 106]. All of that is according to the interests (masalih) that accord with each time, for He is the All-Knowing of everything, and He is the Doer of whatever He wills, with none to object to Him. Al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, said in al-Risalah: He effaces the obligation of whatever He wills and establishes the obligation of whatever He wills.

The retention of the waw in "yamhu" (yamhuw) in all the copies of the Qur'an indicates, by what the people of Allah (ahl Allah) have mentioned, that the waw means elevation and exaltation, that some of what is effaced leaves traces that stand high. For He may efface a person's lifespan after he had fine traces, so He keeps them, spreads them and raises them up, glorified is He. He may efface a law by abrogating it and leave from it good traces that point to the law that replaced it, which has been established. As for its deletion in all the copies, also, in ﴿Allah effaces falsehood﴾ [al-Shura: 24] in al-Shura, although it is likewise in the nominative, it is for the good tidings of the annihilation of falsehood, an annihilation that is the ultimate, as will come, God willing, exalted is He. That is because the verb resembles the command that necessitates the inevitability of execution with utmost perfection and firmness.

He said: ﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾ [al-Ra'd: 43] along with that, i.e., the origin (asl) of ﴿the Book﴾, for whoever's imagination is restricted to the notion that preservation is by writing; it is the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), which is the origin of every book. It has been mentioned more than once before that it is the Clear Book (al-Kitab al-Mubin), which is such that it clarifies everything whose knowledge is sought from it whenever it is sought. Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him and his father, said: "They are two books: a book other than the Mother of the Book, from which He effaces whatever He wills and establishes, and the Mother of the Book, from which nothing is changed." End of quote.

The meaning, and Allah knows best, is that in the Mother of the Book it is written that "We will do such-and-such," even though in the branch (al-far') it is otherwise. This is in relation to one law rather than another: when the first law is annulled, then We efface it at such-and-such a term. Or the meaning is: He effaces from that Book whatever He wills by causing its content to cease to exist after it had been brought into being, and establishes whatever He wills by bringing it into existence from non-existence, while the Mother of the Book is with Him. Al-Razi said in al-Lawami': "They have said much about this. In general, everything that the will (mashi'ah) relates to among created beings is between effacement and establishment: effacement in relation to the form that has been lifted, establishment in relation to the second form. The eternal decree (al-qada' al-azali) and the divine will (al-mashi'ah al-rabbaniyyah) are the source of this effacement and establishment. Therefore that is the qada', and this is the qadar. So qada' is the source of qadar, and qadar is the manifestation of qada'. Allah, exalted is He, and His attributes are free from change."

(p-٣٦٣) When he had completed what he intended concerning their harmony, and concluded that He, glorified is He, does what He wills of advancing and delaying, erasing and affirming, and when among their suggestions and demands was the mocking request to hasten the evil they had been threatened with, and the self sometimes wished that this would occur for some and be affirmed so that others would believe, in order to bring about the settling of the dispute, He, glorified and exalted is He, said: ﴿And whether We show you﴾. He emphasized it to stress the informing that there is no blame on him for the straying of those who strayed [after] his delivery of the message, negating what the intense mercy and compassion he had for them might lead him to, namely the supposition that it was incumbent upon him to bring them back to the truth necessarily. ﴿Some of what We promise them﴾ while you are alive, of what you or your companions desire. He separated the matter by it, so its occurrence was established as a confirmation of the eyes of you [believers] before your death. The promise (waʿd) is the report of a good that is guaranteed, and the threat (waʿīd) is the report of an evil that is guaranteed, and the meaning here is the latter, and He named it a promise because of their treating it, in seeking its descent, as if it were a promise. ﴿Or We take you back﴾ before We show you that. It is one whose effect is erased and has not come to pass. So what is upon you and what is up to Us are equal with respect to both states. ﴿Then upon you is only the delivery﴾ and it is the passing of a thing to its endpoint, and here it is the message. It is not incumbent upon you to fight them, nor to bring them the suggested signs. ﴿And upon Us is the reckoning﴾, and it is the recompense of every doer for what he did in this world and the Hereafter, and We have complete power over it. And the verse (p-٣٦٤) is of the device of ihtibak (a rhetorical figure in which two complementary elements are mentioned and each is omitted from the other's place), as its explanation has passed regarding its like in [Surah Yunus], peace be upon him.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 13, verse 41:

When the context guided us to the conclusion that the implied meaning, in establishing that He, glorified is He, is able to requite whoever He wills, [the verse] "Do they not see that We have destroyed those before them, who were mightier than them in strength and greater in number?" was followed by His saying: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land﴾, that is, by virtue of Our majesty, ﴿the land﴾ in which these disbelievers dwell. It is as if it were said: What kind of coming? It was said: the coming of might when We will, and of mercy when We will. ﴿reducing it﴾, and "naqs" (reduction) means taking a part from a whole so that it becomes less, ﴿from its extremities﴾, by what Allah grants the Muslims of conquest, which adds to the land of the people of Islam, by killing some of the disbelievers and the submission of others, until He destroys its people according to what We know to be wise in the management and alternation of affairs, changing them from state to state until they reach their settled place after the reckoning, in the abode of reward or punishment. This is because the Muslims used to raid the lands adjoining the noble city of Madinah, from the outskirts of the lands of the disbelievers, as Allah, exalted is He, guided by His saying: ﴿Fight those of the disbelievers who are near to you﴾ [al-Tawbah: 123]. So they conquered them one after another, until all the Arabs submitted, willingly or unwillingly, after the killing of their leaders and the humbling of their commanders. ﴿And Allah overrules His affair﴾. "Al-taraf" (extremity) means the furthest limit, which is a place of a thing beyond which there is nothing of it. The extremities of the land are its sides. It was said: "al-atraf" are the dwellings of the nobles, who seek proximity to guests.

Then He affirmed for Himself a universal matter in which this is included. He said, shifting the speech from the style of first-person plural of majesty to the third person, the form of absence which is the greatest of majesty, by the Greatest Name (al-ism al-a'zam, the Greatest Name of Allah): ﴿And Allah﴾, that is, the Supreme King, ﴿judges﴾ what He wills, because ﴿there is no repealer﴾, that is, no one who reverses, because "ta'qib" means returning a thing after it has been separated, ﴿for His judgment﴾. He has decreed victory and ascendancy for Islam, and for disbelief decline and retreat. Whoever judges other than this attribute is not a true judge. This is sufficient to inspire fear of the seizures of His power. ﴿And He is swift in reckoning﴾, while His power is complete, His requital encompasses every deed, and it is inconceivable that anything should escape Him, so the meeting with His requital is inevitable. Everything that is coming is swift. Yet He, with this, reckons for every deed its requital according to what wisdom requires, whether justice or grace, at the moment it is performed. He needs no time in which to consider what its requital is, or whether it was done or not, for nothing hidden is concealed from Him. "Al-sur'ah" (swiftness) is the doing of a thing in a short period as wisdom determines, while "al-ibta'" (slowness) is doing it over a long period beyond what wisdom requires. Swiftness is praiseworthy, and haste ('ajalah) is blameworthy. He, exalted is He, is able over the disbelievers, even if they are as those certain that they will prevail, because of their strength and numbers, together with soundness of opinions, sharpness of thought, and power of wealth, and even if their plotting is intense. He does not avail them anything. ﴿They have plotted against you more than once, but I have only increased you in exaltation﴾.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 13, verse 42:

﴿And those before them had certainly plotted﴾. Since the intended meaning of "the plotters" is only some people at some time, He said: ﴿before them﴾, that is, against the messengers and their followers. So their plotting turned back upon them as a harm. In this clause He omitted their plotting, which they had gathered upon [more than] once and perfected in their own estimation, and which became the cause of the elevation of Islam and its people and the humiliation of polytheism and its people. The omitted part is indicated by the conjunction waw in His words ﴿and certainly﴾. He also omitted from the preceding discourse the destruction of the earlier nations, as evidence of His power to requite, which is the essence of the reckoning, and this is indicated by the conjunction waw in ﴿Have they not seen﴾ [al-Ra'd: 41]. So reflect on this display within the molds of inimitability (i'jaz).

Since this is so, it follows that He said: ﴿So to Allah belongs all plotting﴾, that is, the Supreme King, whose knowledge and power encompass everything, exclusively. Makr (plotting) is turning someone away from their aim through a stratagem, and it entails concealment, as its explanation has passed. Nothing is more hidden from the servants than the acts of the Exalted, so they have no way to know them except through Him, glorified is He. His act is called makr metaphorically, because it arises as a recompense for their plotting. Then He gave the reason for this in His words: ﴿He knows﴾. It is also possible that this is an explanation of what precedes it, since knowledge of the plot by the plotter, who is established in the subtlest plotting without perceiving it, [is what is meant]. ﴿what every soul earns﴾, that is, of plotting and other than it. So He will requite them when He wills, by bringing about from every cause they establish a effect that is the opposite of what they intended. They are not empowered to will anything except by His will. So you will see what befalls them of His might, through your agency or through other means, until you prevail over them and annihilate them entirely. ﴿And the disbelievers will know﴾, that is, every disbeliever, by a promise that does not fail, if he is so ignorant that he knows nothing except through explicit statement or sensory perception, ﴿to whom belongs the final outcome of the abode﴾, when We come to them contrary to what they wanted. And kasb (earning) is an act performed to bring about benefit or to repel harm.

Commentary of al-Biqa'i (Nazm al-Durar) on surah 13, verse 43:

Since His saying, Exalted is He, ﴿And those who disbelieve say, "Why has a sign not been sent down upon him?"﴾ [al-Ra'd: 7], had preceded, it is joined to it, after explaining what it entailed, by His saying: ﴿And those who disbelieve say﴾ [al-Ra'd: 27], meaning they brought disbelief into being, even at its lowest degree, as a saying repeated again and again: ﴿You are not a messenger﴾, because you do not bring their proposed signs, even though he never said that he was able to produce them. So it is as if it was said: "What should I say to them?" Then He said: ﴿Say, "God suffices as a witness between me and you"﴾. (p-368) Sufficiency (al-kifayah) is the existence of a thing in the measure of need. The "bi" in "billah" (by God) means, that is, the One who has complete encompassment, and it serves for emphasis, because the verb could be attributed to other than its doer if it is commanded; this possibility is removed in two respects: the direction of the doer and the direction of turning the attribution. "Witness" (shahidan) means one who is thorough in knowledge in his testimony, through awareness of what has appeared and what has been hidden. ﴿Between me and you﴾: He bears witness to the confirmation of my message and the validation of my claim, by the sign He has shown me and the proof He has made clear through this Book; and He bears witness to your denial, by your claim of the ability to produce its equal and your abandoning of it out of inability. This is according to the degrees of testimony, because testimony is a statement that yields a predominant assumption that the matter is as it is attested, whereas the miracle is a specific act that necessitates certainty that what it came for is as it is. ﴿And whoever has knowledge of the Book﴾, that is, of what He sent down in it of principles and branches, and of the report of what was and what will be, in a manner of styles and a pattern of methods that silenced the eloquent, left the rhetoricians mute, and bewildered the wise. He is God, Exalted is He, as confirmation and verification of my claim. It is supported that the intended meaning is "God" by the reading "min" (of) as a preposition. Placing it in this manner of ambiguity serves to stir the soul toward seeking the one described by this attribute, which is not in a specific designation; it is thus like the claim of a thing accompanied by its proof. Thus this last has coincided with the beginning of the surah, in that what was sent down is true from Him, and that they do not believe. And God is the Granter of success.
